kernelEvidence: Darwin 25.5.0 (XNU): killpg(L, 0) and killpg(L, SIGTERM) both raise PermissionError errno 1 while group L still exists with only an unreaped zombie member, and ProcessLookupError once that zombie is reaped. killpg1 skips SZOMB members and returns EPERM for a POSIX caller when it found none (nfound == 0). Linux still signals zombie members, so this state never reports EPERM there.
confirmedCause: agent_test_runner.close_session polls os.killpg(pgid, 0) right after SIGTERM and then every 20 ms, and catches only ProcessLookupError. The SIGTERMed orphan was reparented to launchd when the worker exited; when a probe lands between the orphan's exit and launchd reaping it, the group holds only a zombie and PermissionError escapes. In process it is raised from close_session line 526 of the original runner; the runner CLI turns it into 'Agent unittest runner refused: PermissionError' with exit code 2 and writes no report. _stop_workers has the same pattern for SIGTERM and SIGKILL. Load widens the window (measured about 1.5 ms at load 9); the actual close_session raised in 10 of 300 orphaned-group calls at load about 9 and 5 of 300 at load about 2.5. The session observer tests feed that original refusal straight into their assertions (in process and through the original CLI) and use the original close_session as orphan cleanup.
fix: Product: _group_present treats EPERM as 'group present, nothing live to signal' and only ESRCH as absent. close_session uses it for the initial probe, SIGTERM, the 1 s probe loop, SIGKILL and a new bounded 2 s probe loop after SIGKILL, returning (False, leaked) instead of raising when the group never reaches ESRCH. _stop_workers catches PermissionError beside ProcessLookupError. Harness: the orphan cleanup uses the current runner's close_session; the in-process original close_session observation and the original CLI run alone get a whole-scenario retry with a fresh orphan, at most three attempts, on exactly EPERM or on exit code 2 with exactly that refusal, removing the refused run's retained fixture root by its recorded generation. Current runner paths never retry.
controlledRegression: agent_tools.tests.test_agent_test_runner_zombie_group (Darwin only). A holder N started inside an owned new-session group L forks member M, moves itself to its own group in the same session and never reaps M until a release file appears (30 s backstops). Runner: the whole beforeimage and the fixed close_session meet M alive (killed by their SIGTERM), M already a zombie, and M a zombie through the whole SIGTERM bound; a pass-through killpg recorder releases N only at the second EPERM probe after SIGTERM or SIGKILL. _stop_workers meets a worker observed live that exits unreaped before its SIGTERM, and a SIGTERM-ignoring worker that exits right after a really expired, shortened grace and before its SIGKILL. Both runner CLIs run a selected test that leaves N and M behind. Harness: the old and new observer cases run with a held member injected into their first orphan session and first original CLI worker only; later orphans have their natural zombie window removed (after SIGTERM the recorder waits for ESRCH; the later CLI child leaves the worker group before it exits), so the RED and GREEN are deterministic.
routineSuite: agent_tools.tests.test_agent_test_runner_zombie_group runs in the affected agent-test stage of the managed pre-push tier on the macOS development host whenever the selector reaches it, including changes to agent_test_runner.py, test_agent_test_session_observer.py, these beforeimages or this provenance. On the Linux Fast Checks shards it is selected but skipped: Linux never reports EPERM for a zombie-only group.
nativeEvidenceLimit: Local owned processes only: no VM, SSH host, guest or product native behavior is involved or claimed. The kernel's zombie-only EPERM is reproduced on the Darwin development host; the launchd reaping latency itself remains host state.
failingEvidence: Unfixed (an isolated clone holding both beforeimages as the live files), in the unsandboxed and the sandbox-exec runner: close_session raises PermissionError errno 1 at line 526 when its own SIGTERM leaves the held member a zombie, and at line 514 for a group that is zombie-only at entry or through the whole SIGTERM bound; _stop_workers raises at line 495 for a worker observed live that exits unreaped before its SIGTERM, and at line 505 for a SIGTERM-ignoring worker that exits after the really expired grace, before its SIGKILL; the runner CLI exits 2 with exactly 'Agent unittest runner refused: PermissionError' and no report.json. The unfixed observer cases fail in the original shapes: ERROR at line 62 from the original close_session line 526, ERROR from that line in the orphan cleanup of the two cleanup-only cases, and FAIL at line 126 with '1 != 2 : Agent unittest runner refused: PermissionError'. Under an owned 12-process CPU burner with two concurrent copies, the unfixed observer module also failed naturally in 1 of 60 runs with the original line 62 / line 526 PermissionError.
passingEvidence: Fixed: close_session returns (True, True) only after the kernel reports ESRCH; the pass-through recorder shows EPERM never taken as absence and, in the SIGKILL case, a group that stayed zombie-only for the whole 1 s SIGTERM bound. _stop_workers reaps the worker with return code 0. The fixed CLI exits 1 with an incomplete report (sessionAbsent false, descendantLeak true, fixture root kept, then removed by its generation). The fixed observer cases pass: one fresh orphan after the original's refusal, a current-runner cleanup that observes the same EPERM and waits for ESRCH, and a refused original CLI run whose fixture root is removed by its generation before one fresh run passes. 22 mutants are killed: each close_session EPERM site made uncaught or taken as absence, a single post-SIGKILL check, the two helper variants, each _stop_workers site, and each harness change reverted separately; an explicit equivalent of the fix passes.
loadEvidence: Fixed tree: the runner's 13 direct consumer modules plus this regression (227 tests) pass in both runners; the observer module plus this regression pass 10 of 10 idle rounds; with an owned 12-process CPU burner (load about 20 to 25) two concurrent copies pass 10 of 10 rounds unsandboxed (with test_agent_test_runner and test_ssh_fresh_fixture_custody), 12 of 12 sandboxed (with test_ssh_fresh_fixture_custody), and the observer module alone 60 of 60. Two sandboxed stress rounds that also ran test_agent_test_runner failed only its unrelated worker-order assertion in test_child_has_unique_temporary_runtime_and_lock_roots, which fails identically on the unfixed tree under the same load.
